text: 1576 Dermatological Drug Groups, p.1576 Antidandruff Drugs, p.1576 Corticosteroids, p.1576 Immune System Modifiers, p.1576 Keratolytics, p.1576 Photosensitisers, p.1576 Pigment Modifiers, p.1576 Retinoids, p.1576 Sunscreens, p.1576 Vitamin D Derivatives, p.1577 Wound Management Agents, p.1577 Topical Drug Administration, p.1577 Management of Dermatological Disorders, p.1577 Acne, p.1577 Alopecia, p.1577 Burns, p.1578 Darier’s disease, p.1578 Dermatitis herpetiformis, p.1578 Drug-induced skin reactions, p.1578 Eczema, p.1579 Epidermolysis bullosa, p.1579 Erythema multiforme, p.1580 Hyperhidrosis, p.1580 Ichthyosis, p.1580 Keratinisation disorders, p.1580 Lichen planus, p.1580 Lichen sclerosus, p.1580 Light-induced skin reactions, p.1580 Drug-induced photosensitivity, p.1581 Photoageing, p.1581 Photosensitivity disorders, p.1581 Pemphigus and pemphigoid, p.1582 Pigmentation disorders, p.1582 Pruritus, p.1582 Psoriasis, p.1583 Pyoderma gangrenosum, p.1583 Rosacea, p.1583 Seborrhoeic dermatitis, p.1584 Toxic epidermal necrolysis, p.1584 Urticaria and angioedema, p.1584 Warts, p.1584 Wounds and ulcers, p.1585 The skin is subject to a very wide range of lesions. Some may be characteristic of specific systemic dis- eases and fade as the disease regresses. Some are caused by specific local infections and are best treated by the appropriate antimicrobial (see Skin Infections in the chapters Antibacterials, p.194, and Antifungals, p.521). The skin is also subject to damage from envi- ronmental hazards. Excessive or prolonged exposure to solar radiation is associated with degenerative changes in the skin (premature ageing of the skin or photoageing, p.1581), actinic (solar) keratoses (which are risk factors or precursors of skin cancers), and ma- lignant neoplasms of the skin (p.672). Some skin disor- ders are adverse effects of therapeutic and other agents, ranging from mild hypersensitivity to the life-threaten- ing Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis (see Drug-induced Skin Reactions, p.1578, and Drug-induced Photosensitivity, p.1581).
